prompt.context: Our client is an international manufacturer of medium and high quality kitchen knives. Chef's Best sells knives in more than 20 countries, with a focus in Latin America, US & Canada, and global emerging economies. Chef's Best produces five types of knives: Steak Knives (used at the table), Butcher Knives (used for chopping meat), Carving Knives (used for carving slices from large pieces of meat), Paring Knives (used for cutting small fruits & vegetables), and Chef's Knives (large all-purpose knives). Chef's Best sells primarily through a direct sales method (individual sales people throughout each region). Chef's Best sales are largest in Mexico, the US, and Brazil.
prompt.question: Chef's Best has had slowing sales growth in the past few years. How can Chef's Best increase revenue growth for the next 5-10 years?

clarifying_info.q: What markets does Chef's Best primarily sell in?
clarifying_info.a: Sales are largest in Mexico, the US, and Brazil.

clarifying_info.q: How does Chef's Best sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: Chef's Best sells primarily through a direct sales method with individual sales people throughout each region.

clarifying_info.q: What types of knives does Chef's Best sell?
clarifying_info.a: Five types: Steak Knives, Butcher Knives, Carving Knives, Paring Knives, and Chef's Knives.

exhibits.title: Overview of Major Markets
exhibits.shows: A table of the 10 major markets showing Revenue, Profits, Market Growth rate (%), and Chef's Best Index to Market for each country. Index to Market is calculated as [(Chef's Best Growth / Market Growth) - 1] * 100.

exhibits.title: Overview of Product Categories
exhibits.shows: A table of product categories showing Revenue, Change in Revenue over the past 5 years, and a decomposition of that change into Market-Driven, Channel-Driven, and Share-Driven components.

exhibits.title: Details of Butcher Knives Category
exhibits.shows: A matrix of Butcher Knife sub-categories (General Purpose, Japanese Design, Ever-Sharp, Titanium Edge, Light Weight, Recycled Steel) showing Chef's Best distribution status (Not Distributed / 10-20% Share / Over 20% Share), Chef's Best Sales by Product mix, Annual Market Growth rate, and positioning tier (High End, Mass Market, Discount).

framework: Market Geography: Identify highest-revenue and highest-profit markets; assess growth vs. market growth to find share gainers vs. losers
Product Portfolio: Analyze each knife category for revenue, growth, and share trends to prioritize investment
Distribution Channel: Evaluate direct sales vs. retail distribution effectiveness by category and market
Competitive Position: Understand why Chef's Best is losing share in key markets (Mexico, US) relative to market growth
Growth Levers: Organic share recovery in core markets, product category investment, channel expansion, and emerging market capture

questions.prompt: Phase 1 – Initial Framework: How would you approach the problem of growing Chef's Best revenue over the next 5-10 years?
questions.guidance: A strong framework covers major areas such as product (which categories to grow), customer/market (which geographies to prioritize), company (sales channels and capabilities), and competition (why share is being lost). Creativity and logical structure matter more than a textbook framework here. The interviewer is testing depth and ability to derive a logical approach from ambiguous information.

questions.prompt: Phase 2 – Market Math: Using Exhibit 1, if Chef's Best has 23% market share in Mexico and grows at the same rate as last year in the next year, what will market share be in 1 year? Calculate to 1 decimal place.
questions.guidance: Candidate must identify Chef's Best growth rate from the Index to Market (-70), derive the absolute growth rate, then compute the new market share. Key steps: interpret Index to Market correctly, apply compound growth, and perform the division accurately under pressure. Recover from arithmetic mistakes cleanly.

math.setup: Index to Market = [(Chef's Best Growth / Market Growth) - 1] * 100 = -70. Mexico Market Growth = 7%. Solve for Chef's Best Growth rate, then compute new market share as (23% * (1 + Chef's Best Growth)) / (100% * 1.07).
steps: Step 1: Solve for Chef's Best growth rate: -70/100 = (x/7) - 1 => -0.7 = x/7 - 1 => 0.3 = x/7 => x = 2.1%. Chef's Best grows at 2.1%.
Step 2: New Chef's Best revenue index = 23% * 1.021 = 23.483%
math.answer: Approximately 21.9% market share in Mexico after 1 year.

questions.prompt: Phase 3 – Product Category Analysis: What does Exhibit 2 tell you about what is driving market share changes, and what areas should Chef's Best focus on?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies: (1) Chef's Best is losing share across all categories (Share Driven column is negative for all). (2) Butcher Knives is the most critical issue — it has both a large negative Channel-Driven component (-46) AND an enormous Share-Driven loss (-113), despite a very large Market-Driven tailwind (+186). The market is growing fast but Chef's Best is losing distribution AND share. Candidate should prioritize Butcher Knives as the primary focus area.

questions.prompt: Phase 4 – Butcher Knives Deep Dive: What does Exhibit 3 reveal about the Butcher Knives category, and what should Chef's Best do?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies: (1) Overall fast market growth (weighted growth across sub-categories). (2) Chef's Best is not distributed at all in Recycled Steel (12% annual growth — fastest growing sub-category) and has only 10-20% share in General Purpose (9% growth) and Japanese Design (11% growth). (3) The existing direct sales model is failing — retail distribution is needed to capture growth. (4) Specific recommendations: invest to gain distribution in Recycled Steel, expand share in Japanese Design and General Purpose, and consider shifting from direct sales to retail channel for these higher-growth sub-categories.

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm how Chef's Best can increase revenue growth over the next 5-10 years across all dimensions of the business.

categories.name: Market / Geography
ideas: Defend and grow share in Mexico (largest revenue and profit market)
Re-accelerate growth in US to match or beat market
Expand in high-growth emerging markets: Argentina, Russia, Venezuela, Colombia
Invest disproportionately where index to market is positive (Brazil, Argentina, Japan, Colombia, Venezuela)

categories.name: Product Portfolio
ideas: Prioritize Butcher Knives investment given large market tailwind and significant share/channel losses
Defend Steak Knives share (largest revenue category, share loss of -30)
Evaluate and invest in Recycled Steel and Japanese Design sub-categories with highest market growth
Reduce investment in slow-growth / low-share sub-categories like Light Weight (1% growth)

categories.name: Distribution Channel
ideas: Shift away from direct sales model toward retail distribution, especially for Butcher Knives
Open negotiations with retail distributors to gain shelf space
Diversify channel mix to reduce reliance on costlier direct sales
Pilot retail distribution in high-growth markets where direct sales coverage is thin

categories.name: Competitive Strategy
ideas: Conduct competitive analysis in Mexico and US to identify specific causes of underperformance
Assess whether pricing, quality, or brand awareness is driving share loss
Benchmark competitor distribution strategies in Butcher Knives category

categories.name: Emerging Markets
ideas: Invest in high-growth emerging economies (Russia 22.1%, Venezuela 25.8%, Argentina 16.2%)
Adapt product mix and pricing to local market needs
Establish distribution partnerships to enter markets where direct sales is not viable

recommendation: Focus on recovering share in Mexico and the US, which together represent the largest revenue and profit base — losing further share in these core markets would erode scale economies and competitive position

Invest aggressively in the Butcher Knives category: the market is growing rapidly (+186 market-driven impact) but Chef's Best is losing both distribution and share; this is the single largest growth opportunity
Begin transitioning from a direct sales model to retail distribution, particularly in high-growth categories and markets where direct sales coverage is insufficient
risks: Continued share loss in Mexico (largest profit center) could accelerate if not addressed quickly
Investing in emerging markets without stabilizing core markets may dilute resources and management attention
Shifting to retail distribution may face channel conflict with existing direct sales force
next_steps: Open negotiations with retail distributors to identify paths to expanded distribution for Butcher Knives
Conduct competitive analysis in Mexico and the US to identify specific root causes of underperformance vs. market growth
Prepare financial investment plans for the Butcher Knives category, including distribution expansion for Recycled Steel, Japanese Design, and General Purpose sub-categories
Develop a phased roadmap for transitioning a portion of the sales model from direct to retail distribution
